reader.requirement: At --std 85, after a successful REWRITE the released record need not remain in the record area (its content is then undefined), but when the file is named in a SAME RECORD AREA clause the released record stays available in the record area and as a record of every other file of that clause, whatever the record descriptions (fixed, group, elementary, OCCURS DEPENDING ON).

edition-consulted.switches: the OPEN's default sharing mode read by the REWRITE's lock step; inert for this rule at 85

reader.notes: Character-window records of a SAME RECORD AREA share one backing, so the released record is in every peer for free; an out-of-line record gets an emitted store after a successful REWRITE only. Without SAME RECORD AREA the area keeps its content, which the undefined 'no longer available' permits.

refuter.evidence: Read SequentialIoEmitter.EmitRewrite/BeginReleasedRecord/EndReleasedRecord/ReleasedRecordNeedsAlsoAvailable and FileModel.IsOutOfLineRecord. q4sra.cob at --std 85, SAME RECORD AREA FOR FA FB FC FD1 with an alphanumeric record, an elementary numeric DISPLAY record, an elementary COMP-3 record and a group with COMP-3: REWRITE FB-REC (5678) -> FA-REC=5678; REWRITE FC-NUM FROM WS-NUM -> FD-NUM=-7654321; REWRITE FA-REC NEW2 -> FB-REC=NEW2. Without SAME RECORD AREA the 'no longer available' content is undefined, so the kept content cannot overturn. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.4.5.4 GR3 'also available to the program as a record of other files referenced in the same SAME RECORD AREA clause'.
